definitions.explanation: An optical phenomenon where light bends through layers of air at different temperatures, creating the appearance of distant objects being displaced or inverted, or the illusion of water in deserts.

examples.japanese: ⟦{砂漠|さばく}→砂漠：09508_sabaku⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{蜃気楼|しんきろう}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{見|み}た→見る：00283_miru⟧。
examples.english: I saw a mirage in the desert.

examples.japanese: {富山湾|とやまわん}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{蜃気楼|しんきろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{名所|めいしょ}→名所：08164_meisho⟧⟦として→として：06802_toshite⟧⟦{有名|ゆうめい}→有名：01106_yuumei⟧⟦だ→だ：09496_da⟧。
examples.english: Toyama Bay is famous as a spot for viewing mirages.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{計画|けいかく}→計画：01172_keikaku⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{蜃気楼|しんきろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ように→よう：01114_you⟧⟦{消|き}えた→消える：02520_kieru⟧。
examples.english: That plan vanished like a mirage.

notes:
KANJI ORIGIN:
・{蜃|しん} (giant clam) + {気|き} (vapor) + {楼|ろう} (tower)
・Ancient Chinese believed giant clams breathed out vapor that formed phantom towers
・This mythology gave the phenomenon its name

TYPES:
・⟦{上位|じょうい}→上位：11188_joui⟧{蜃気楼|しんきろう} (superior mirage - objects appear elevated)
・⟦{下位|かい}→下位：11710_kai⟧{蜃気楼|しんきろう} (inferior mirage - objects appear below actual position)
・⟦{逃|に}げ{水|みず}→逃げ水：29993_nigemizu⟧ (road mirage - appearance of water on hot roads)

FAMOUS VIEWING SPOTS IN JAPAN:
・⟦{富山県|とやまけん}→富山県：28947_toyamaken⟧{魚津市|うおづし} (Uozu, Toyama) - most famous
・Spring (April-May) is best viewing season
・{蜃気楼|しんきろう}ロード (Mirage Road) is a designated viewing area

SCIENTIFIC CAUSE:
・Temperature difference between air layers
・Light refraction creates distorted images

FIGURATIVE USE:
・Something illusory or unattainable
・{蜃気楼|しんきろう}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦ような→よう：01114_you⟧⟦{夢|ゆめ}→夢：01519_yume⟧ (an illusory dream)
